subject: Post-call: aligning index growth and inference budgets
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Rao <maya@datascout.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 14:32:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: aligning index growth and inference budgets

Hi Maya — great to meet today, thanks for the detailed walkthrough of DataScout's rerank flow. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of what you shared
- Index size today: ~120M vectors (300–512 dim, dense), growing ~15% month-over-month.
- Current vector DB: Weaviate (managed in-house) with hnsw + disk offload; hybrid text + embedding pipeline.
- Traffic profile: ~250k real-time queries/day (70% single-query low-latency; 30% batched offline reranks up to 5k q/day).
- Re-rank pattern: initial candidate retrieval (approx 2k candidates), then model-based rerank on top 100 candidates for personalization.
- Current pain: p99 rerank latency spikes (300–600ms), unpredictable costs for peak windows, and manual index compaction causing downtime during bulk updates.

Goals you stated
- Target p95/p99 latency for rerank under 120ms / 250ms respectively for real-time traffic.
- Keep monthly inference spend for reranking under ~$6k (pilot target) while supporting index growth to 200M vectors within 6 months.
- Reduce manual ops for nightly/weekly maintenance and enable safe canary/model rollouts.

Redwood engagement opportunities we discussed
- Model variant routing: fall back to lighter quantized variants during spikes to preserve latency SLOs.
- Prefix/KV caching for personalization keys to reduce repeated KV cost on hot users.
- Batching + async rerank for non-interactive traffic (the 30% batch window) to move heavy compute away from low-latency path.
- Guidance on quantization and kernel selection that preserves hit-rate at lower compute cost.

Suggested success criteria (proposal)
- Functional: 95% of queries return a reranked top-10 within 250ms; 80% within 120ms for targeted flows.
- Cost: per-query rerank cost < $0.002 (pilot target) and monthly pilot spend <= $6,000.
- Ops: zero scheduled downtime for compaction; canary rollout capability for model/re-rank logic.

Immediate next steps
1) I'll loop in Rishi (SE) and Laura (AE) to put together a short pilot plan + rough TCO model (configuration options: dedicated pool vs hosted autoscale, quantized 8-bit vs 4-bit variants).
2) Could you share: (a) a small sample of index stats (percentiles for vector dimensions, typical candidate set sizes), and (b) a redacted query traffic histogram (hourly qps) so we can size pools?
3) We'll deliver a 1‑page pilot proposal + cost envelope by EOD Thursday (2026-09-09).

Attachments: call_notes_datascout_20260907.pdf (call notes), redwood_tco_example_datascout.xlsx (sample TCO model).

Thanks — Hannah

Hannah Schmitt

- Index growth: 15% MoM is accurate, but we have an on-prem ingestion spike scheduled for mid-October that could accelerate that to ~25% for a couple of weeks.
- Candidates: typical candidate set is 1.8k median, 2.4k 95th, but very spiky on taxonomy imports.
- Traffic: we have clear diurnal patterns and weekday peaks (~2.8x difference). We can provide the histogram in CSV (anonymized).

If you can send the pilot proposal and the sample TCO before EOD Thursday that would be excellent; we'll try to have the infra lead (cc'd on the next message) review.

Looping you both in to scope a pilot. Key asks and constraints from DataScout (Maya):
- Index today ~120M vectors; possible short-term 25% growth spike in Oct.
- Target: keep pilot spend <= $6k/mo; per-query rerank target < $0.002.
- Latency SLOs: p95/p99 goals 120ms / 250ms for the main interactive workflow.
- Traffic shape: strong diurnal patterns; 30% of traffic can be batched/async.

Suggested approach (quick):
1) Run a 6-week pilot on a small dedicated pool with autoscaling headroom + cache layer. Include 2 variants: optimized quantized (8-bit) and fallback 4-bit during spikes.
2) Use prefix/KV caching for the top 10% of active users to reduce repeated costs.
3) Move non-interactive reranks into an async batch job during off-peak windows.

Attachments: call_notes_datascout_20260907.pdf, redwood_tco_example_datascout.xlsx

Can you take point on: (A) sizing (Rishi) and (B) commercial pilot proposal (Laura)? I'd like a one-page summary + cost envelope + a short list of required infra access (sample metrics CSV, candidate-size distribution) by EOD Thursday.

Thanks — Hannah
